instruction: On Budget's car rental website, search for a one-day car rental at Boston Logan Intl Airport from June 10 to June 11, 2026.

All three instruction requirements are covered: pickup date (.*pickupDate=2026-06-10.*), dropoff date (.*dropoffDate=2026-06-11.*), and airport location (.*pickupLocation=.*Boston.*Logan.*).

Parameter handling is correct: is_expected_url_pattern_match accesses rules['expected'] directly, which is consistent with expected.type='rule' causing the framework to pass the rules dict (config['rules']) directly as the second argument.
The location regex '.*pickupLocation=.*Boston.*Logan.*' correctly matches URL-encoded forms like 'Boston+Logan+Intl+Airport' as confirmed by the actual budget.com URL format in task_rationale.
Negative control resistance is satisfied: the initial budget.com homepage URL has no query parameters, so none of the three patterns would match the initial state.
The previous coverage gap (missing location pattern) has been fixed by adding the third regex pattern '.*pickupLocation=.*Boston.*Logan.*'.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent on budget.com set location to Boston Logan but failed at calendar date selection, never successfully setting June 10-11 before the 50-turn limit.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome, fill in location search fields, interact with calendar date pickers (with difficulty)
metadata.failure_analysis: Agent could not accurately click the correct calendar cells for June 10 and June 11 due to coordinate confusion in the two-month calendar layout. This is the core failure sub-goal.
metadata.task_rationale: The original failure target — setting both June 10 and June 11 dates — is the exact point where the agent broke down. As a simplified version, this task removes the sorting requirement and focuses only on filling both date fields correctly. The URL in screenshot 45 confirmed this state: budget.com/en/home?pickupLocation=Boston+Logan+Intl+Airport&pickupDate=2026-06-10&dropoffDate=2026-06-11
metadata.explanation: Evaluator checks that pickupDate=2026-06-10, dropoffDate=2026-06-11, and pickupLocation containing 'Boston Logan' all appear in the URL. Budget.com encodes location and dates in the query string after they are selected. The initial state (budget.com homepage) does not have these params, ensuring negative-control resistance. [Fixed: added third regex pattern '.*pickupLocation=.*Boston.*Logan.*' to verify the airport location, preventing false positives from correct dates at a wrong airport.]
fix_history: Fix 1: Added third regex pattern '.*pickupLocation=.*Boston.*Logan.*' to expected patterns to verify Boston Logan Intl Airport is selected, closing the coverage gap where correct dates at a wrong airport would incorrectly pass.
